title: Audit entries without side effects in the pipeline

blocks.text: A lambda inside `filter` or `map` should compute, not change things outside itself. A counter bumped inside `filter` counts what the filter *looked at*, and a counter bumped inside `peek` may never run at all: since Java 9, `list.stream().peek(...).count()` can answer from the list's size without running `peek`. Collect the result, then measure it.
The file declares `record Entry(String id, boolean valid)` and `record Report(List<String> validIds, long validCount, long seen)`. Write `static Report audit(List<Entry> entries)` in `Audit`:

items: `validIds`: the ids of the valid entries, in order;
`seen`: how many entries there are in all.

blocks.text: Each number must be right on its own; no lambda in your pipeline needs to touch a variable outside it.

cases.says: The report lists the ids of the valid entries, in order.
validCount counts the entries that passed, not every entry the filter looked at.
seen counts every entry; a counter bumped inside peek can be skipped when count() already knows the size.

concepts: Lambdas in filter and map compute without changing outside state; results are collected, then measured.
A stream may skip peek entirely, so peek is for debugging and never for work that must happen.
